text: The Premier League Player of the Month is an award that recognises the best-performing player each month of the season. The winner is determined by a combination of a public online vote (contributing 10% of the total), a panel of experts, and the captain of each Premier League club. The award has had several name changes: it was known as the Carling Premiership Player of the Month from 1994 to 2001, the Barclaycard Premiership Player of the Month from 2001 to 2004, the Barclays Player of the Month from 2004 to 2016, and is currently called the EA Sports Player of the Month. The Premier League was established in 1992 when the First Division clubs withdrew from the Football League to form a commercially independent league with its own broadcast and sponsorship agreements. New Manager of the Month and Manager of the Season awards were introduced for the 1993–94 season, alongside existing Football Writers' Association and Professional Footballers' Association Player of the Year awards. The Player of the Month award was first introduced for the 1994–95 season and was first awarded to Tottenham Hotspur's Jürgen Klinsmann in August 1994. Sergio Agüero, Harry Kane, and Mohamed Salah have each won the award seven times, the most among all players. Nine players have won the award in consecutive months: Robbie Fowler, Dennis Bergkamp, Cristiano Ronaldo, Harry Kane, Jamie Vardy, Mohamed Salah, Bruno Fernandes, İlkay Gündoğan, and Marcus Rashford. Only Mohamed Salah and Marcus Rashford have won the award three times in a single season, and Fernandes is the first player to win four awards in one calendar year. Nineteen individuals have won two awards in a season, including Robbie Fowler, Dennis Bergkamp, Ruud van Nistelrooy, Thierry Henry, Wayne Rooney, Ryan Giggs, Cristiano Ronaldo, Ashley Young, Peter Odemwingie, Robin van Persie, Daniel Sturridge, Luis Suárez, Harry Kane, Jamie Vardy, Sergio Agüero, Son Heung-min, Bruno Fernandes, Erling Haaland, and Mohamed Salah. Robbie Keane is the only player to have won the award while playing for three clubs, and twelve players have won it while playing for two clubs: Alan Shearer, Dion Dublin, David Ginola, Dwight Yorke, Tim Flowers, Teddy Sheringham, Danny Murphy, Andrew Johnson, Nicolas Anelka, Dimitar Berbatov, Scott Parker, and Robin van Persie. The award has been shared six times: between Blackburn Rovers's Alan Shearer and Chris Sutton in November 1994, Liverpool's Robbie Fowler and Stan Collymore in January 1996, Southampton's Kevin Davies and Manchester United's Andy Cole in November 1997, Arsenal's Dennis Bergkamp and Edu in February 2004, Tottenham Hotspur's Dimitar Berbatov and Robbie Keane in April 2007, and Liverpool's Steven Gerrard and Luis Suárez in April 2014. More than four in ten of the Player of the Month awards have gone to English players, and about a fifth of foreign winners have been French or Dutch. Michail Antonio became the first player to win the award with different nationalities, winning in July 2020 as an Englishman and in August 2021 as a Jamaican. Manchester United has had more Player of the Month awards than any other club. As of December 2025, the latest winner is Leeds United forward Dominic Calvert-Lewin. The award has been given monthly from the 1994–95 season through to the 2025–26 season, covering the following seasons: 1994–95, 1995–96, 1996–97, 1997–98, 1998–99, 1999–2000, 2000–01, 2001–02, 2002–03, 2003–04, 2004–05, 2005–06, 2006–07, 2007–08, 2008–09, 2009–10, 2010–11, 2011–12, 2012–13, 2013–14, 2014–15, 2015–16, 2016–17, 2017–18, 2018–19, 2019–20, 2020–21, 2021–22, 2022–23, 2023–24, 2024–25, and 2025–26. A table lists the number of awards won by players who have won at least two Player of the Month awards. Players in bold are still active in the Premier League, and players in italics are still active in professional football outside of the Premier League.
